text:
Alex R: Hey — I have a set of nsys + perfetto traces from a perf regression on the LlamaX inference path. Where should I upload and what's our redaction + naming standard?
Priya N: Upload to the central perf traces bucket by default. For customer-sensitive runs use s3://redwood-perf-traces/private/ (KMS-encrypted). For internal synthetic runs use s3://redwood-perf-traces/internal/. Do NOT put PII or prompt text in the root trace.
Sam T: quick :+1: If you want a sharable perf bundle (nsys + perfetto + metadata) use the perf-bundles layout we discussed last quarter. One tar with scrubbed traces + metadata.json.
Marta L: Redaction checklist: remove prompt text, user IDs, IPs, raw filepaths with /home/ or /mnt/ that contain customer names, and any API keys. If the trace includes logs with requests, redact the body.
Alex R: can you paste an example naming convention?
Priya N: Our recommended name: <team>_<model>_<kernelset>_<batchshape>_<runid>_<YYYYMMDD>. Example: runtime_llamaX_fusedAttn_v2_bs8x2048_r123_20260309.nsight.tar.gz
Priya N: Minimal metadata to include (plain text file called metadata.txt or metadata.json inside the tar): model, model_version, commit_sha, kernel_set (e.g. fusedAttn-v2), sequence_length, batch_shape, batch_size, kv_cache_policy, batching_policy, gpu_type, driver+cuda versions, reproduce_command, perf_hypothesis, any regression ticket link. Keep it concise.
Sam T: For generating traces, these commands are handy. nsys (CLI) capture example:
```
nsys profile -o runtime_llamaX_r123 --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none --force-overwrite --record-flags=none --sleep=1 -- python -u run_inference.py --model ..
```
For perfetto (if you need a perfetto proto or HTML): run the trace conversion after nsys export: `nsys export -f us -o trace.sqlite runtime_llamaX_r123.qdrep` -> convert to perfetto via internal script.
Marta L: reminder: use NVTX markers in the code to mark batching boundaries and KV cache hits/misses — it makes hotspot correlation trivial in perfetto. Something like:
```
NVTX_PUSH("BATCH_START size=8 seq=2048")
// dispatch
NVTX_POP()
NVTX_PUSH("KV_CACHE_HIT shard=3")
NVTX_POP()
```
Alex R: For scrub scripts, do we have a canonical one?
perf-bot: Uploaded scrub_trace.py to s3://redwood-tools/perf-tools/scrub_trace.py (version 2026-01-12). Use the --redact-prompts and --strip-paths flags.
Priya N: Example scrub + package flow (run from CI or your laptop):
```
python scrub_trace.py --input runtime_llamaX_r123.qdrep --output runtime_llamaX_r123.scrub.qdrep --redact-prompts --strip-paths --strip-ips
mkdir -p tmp_bundle && cp runtime_llamaX_r123.scrub.qdrep tmp_bundle/
cat > tmp_bundle/metadata.txt <<EOF
model: llamaX
model_version: v3.2
commit: ab12cd34
kernel_set: fusedAttn-v2
batch_shape: bs8x2048
kv_cache_policy: prefix-cache-on
gpu: a100-sxm4
notes: saw 12% regression vs baseline commit ab12ab12
EOF
tar -czvf runtime_llamaX_fusedAttn_v2_bs8x2048_r123_20260309.tar.gz -C tmp_bundle .
aws s3 cp runtime_llamaX_fusedAttn_v2_bs8x2048_r123_20260309.tar.gz s3://redwood-perf-traces/internal/
```
Sam T: When you upload, set S3 metadata tags: `x-amz-meta-redwood-team: runtime`, `x-amz-meta-regression-ticket: PERF-4321`, and for private uploads add `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` + `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id: arn:aws:kms:...`
Alex R: What level of detail to include for kernel-selection notes?
Priya N: Include which kernel set was active and any runtime decisions: e.g., fallback to matmul-only kernels at seq>4096, quantized-kernel-priority, or if graph fusion was disabled. Add the runtime logs snippet that shows the kernel selection decision (scrub filepaths but keep the decision line).
Marta L: For KV cache behavior include a little table in metadata: total_tokens, avg_kv_hit_rate, eviction_count, cache_policy. That helps correlate perf spikes with cache thrashing.
Alex R: How do we annotate traces for the SRE/infra folks so they can link it to an infra event?
Sam T: Add a top-level README inside the bundle with: timestamp, machine hostname (scrub real hostnames if they embed customer names), kernel drivers, and the nvprof/nsys invocation line. Also add pointer to the perf regression issue and the trace S3 path. Use the `@infra` tag in the regression ticket so infra gets notified.
Priya N: If the trace contains customer queries we can't fully scrub (edge case), request a private storage workflow: create a ticket to infra with the trace owner + customer owner, request short-lived access for reviewers, and specify the KMS key. Docs: https://intranet.redwood/ops/perf-trace-handling (internal-only).
Alex R: any quick tips for hotspot identification?
Sam T: In nsight compute/visualizer look for kernels with \u226530% of GPU time and long host-to-device memcpy peaks. In perfetto, inspect GPU slices by timeline and correlate NVTX markers around batch dispatch. Typical culprits: large matmuls, fused_attention, cuda memset when kv cache reallocation occurs.
Marta L: If you find a kernel selection regression (new kernel slower than old), include both qdrep files: baseline.qdrep + current.qdrep and the short reproduce script that toggles kernel flags so eng-runtime can A/B.
Alex R: perfect — I'll scrub + package and upload to internal bucket, ping PERF-4321 and @priya when done. Thanks all :rocket:
perf-bot: Reminder: uploads to s3://redwood-perf-traces/private require ticket attachment and dataplane-owner approval.
